---
title: "About MLPerf EDU"
---

MLPerf EDU is an independent pedagogical ML systems benchmark preview
developed alongside the [Machine Learning Systems](https://mlsysbook.ai)
textbook. It draws methodological inspiration from
[MLCommons MLPerf](https://mlcommons.org/benchmarks/) but is not an official
MLCommons benchmark and is not endorsed by MLCommons.

## Design Philosophy

**Authoritative workload inheritance.** Each score-bearing definition starts
from an established upstream model, dataset split, evaluator, and quality
reference. The project contributes only the PyTorch adapter, measurement
harness, quality gate, provenance, and reports needed for local execution.

**Traceable lineage.** Workloads identify their model, dataset, scenario,
runner, and research lineage. Public-result candidates add structured asset
dossiers and review packets.

**Introspection for teaching.** The harness records systems telemetry such as
arithmetic intensity, data-loading behavior, and estimated energy when the
platform supports it. Students can change controlled configurations without
changing the benchmark's workload identity.

**Reviewable provenance.** Runs emit reports and provenance manifests that bind
results to source, assets, configuration, and environment evidence. Training
and inference workloads can share checkpoint lineage when the registry
declares that dependency.

**Canonical and classroom paths.** Registered workloads produce artifacts for
the benchmark validation path. The three labs are standalone educational
experiments; only [Lab 2](guide/sut-plugins.qmd) demonstrates the repository's
`SUT_Interface`, and it drives that interface locally rather than through the
product CLI.

## Profiles as a Contract

`min` provides functional confidence. `max` runs the authoritative quality
contract in its declared environment, and `pro` exposes the research envelope.
A profile alone does not make a result
publishable. Quality evidence, release validation, asset policy, and result
wording must also pass the applicable gates. The
[running guide](guide/running.qmd) documents the current semantics.

## Single Source of Truth

Every generated benchmark page comes from the
[workload registry](https://github.com/harvard-edge/cs249r_book/tree/main/mlperf-edu/registry),
which is also consumed by the harness. The CLI reference comes from the CLI's
own help output. CI fails when native registry files, compatibility mirrors,
review packets, or generated documentation drift.

## Status and Governance

The repository contains the public-result rules, dataset release review,
quality-target review, release checklist, and proposed MLCommons review path.
The current external gates include expert target review, an authoritative
component license for package publication, package-index publication, and
MLCommons decisions about naming and result wording.

Development happens in the
[cs249r_book repository](https://github.com/harvard-edge/cs249r_book). Feedback
is welcome on the
[issue tracker](https://github.com/harvard-edge/cs249r_book/issues).

## Citing

The draft companion paper, *MLPerf EDU: Bridging Industry Benchmarking and ML
Systems Education*, lives under
[`paper/`](https://github.com/harvard-edge/cs249r_book/tree/main/mlperf-edu/paper).
It is not yet an archival benchmark citation. A stable citation will accompany
a reviewed release.
